correctness.rationale: The exact-two operation includes a second operation on a new symbol, so the canonical labels are P(i,j), A(i), B(i), with n(n+3)/2 labels. For equal outputs with different first marked sites, let i be the earlier site and c the complement of x_i. Equality forces a following run c^v with v≥1. The later-marked output has at most v consecutive c's after x_i. The earlier B(i) has v+2 and is impossible. An earlier P(i,j) can match only if j is inside the run but not at its end (otherwise the c-prefix exceeds v); replace it by A(j+1). An earlier A(i) can be replaced by A(i+1). These moves strictly advance the first marked site. At a common first site, A and B differ immediately, and P cannot match either: equality of a single suffix duplication with prepending a letter c would require the unchanged prefix through the marked letter and its inserted complement to both equal c. Two P labels with a shared first mark match only if their second marks agree, by the same single-insertion comparison. Thus the stated collisions exhaust the possibilities. A-to-A edges are a subpath and P vertices attach as leaves; the number of edges lost is the weighted complementary-run sum. Independent run sums give the rational series and extrema, including the n=1 base case. A fresh direct sequential-output enumeration plus a per-letter two-state histogram verified 35,268 words, including the reported q=4, n=6 coefficients.
